title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 15.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He rose again the third day
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Corinthians 15:3 where it says, 'how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;' indicating this event occurs first in the narrative.

questions.question: What is the gospel that Paul preached according to 1 Corinthians 15?
options: That Christ rose from the dead
That Christ died for our sins
That Christ was seen of Cephas
questions.correctAnswer: That Christ died for our sins
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 15:3, Paul declares the gospel, stating 'how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;' which is a central tenet of the gospel he preached.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:4, what happened on the third day?
options: Christ was seen of the apostles
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:4 states, 'and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:' indicating this event occurred on the third day.

questions.question: Who was seen first after Christ's resurrection according to 1 Corinthians 15?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:5 states, 'And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:' indicating Cephas was seen first.

questions.question: How many brethren did Christ appear to at once according to 1 Corinthians 15:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:6 mentions, 'he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once;' which specifies the number of brethren present.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the least of the apostles in 1 Corinthians 15?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 15:9, Paul states, 'For I am the least of the apostles,' indicating he considers himself the least.

questions.question: What does Paul attribute his labor to in 1 Corinthians 15:10?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:10 states, 'But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain;' attributing his labor to grace.

questions.question: What is the consequence if there is no resurrection of the dead according to 1 Corinthians 15:13?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:13 states, 'But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen:' which directly indicates the consequence of no resurrection.

questions.question: What happens to those who have fallen asleep in Christ if there is no resurrection according to 1 Corinthians 15:18?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:18 states, 'Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished;' highlighting the fate of those who have died in Christ if there is no resurrection.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:19, if we have hope in Christ only in this life, what are we?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:19 states, 'If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable;' indicating a bleak outlook without hope beyond this life.

questions.question: What has Christ become according to 1 Corinthians 15:20?
options: The firstfruits of them that slept
questions.correctAnswer: The firstfruits of them that slept
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:20 states, 'But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept;' indicating his role as the firstfruits.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul preached the resurrection of Christ according to the text?
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in 1 Corinthians 15:12, where it mentions 'Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead...'

questions.question: Is it true that Paul said he labored more abundantly than all the apostles?
questions.explanation: This is true according to 1 Corinthians 15:10, where Paul states, 'but I laboured more abundantly than they all:'

questions.question: Is it true that the text states Christ was seen only by the apostles?
questions.explanation: This is false; 1 Corinthians 15:6 states he was seen by above five hundred brethren, not just the apostles.

questions.question: Is it true that Christ was not raised according to the text?
questions.explanation: This is false; 1 Corinthians 15:20 confirms 'But now is Christ risen from the dead,' affirming his resurrection.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:21, what came by man?
options: Death and the resurrection of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Death and the resurrection of the dead
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:21 states, 'For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.' This shows both death and resurrection came by man.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 15:22 promise will happen if someone is in Christ as described in 1 Corinthians 15:21?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:22 says, 'For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive,' directly promising life to those in Christ as contrasted with death through Adam.

questions.question: What is described as the order in which resurrection occurs in 1 Corinthians 15:23?
options: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming
All at once at the end of time
The angels first, then the saints
questions.correctAnswer: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:23 explains resurrection happens in order: 'Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.'

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:24-25, what must happen before Christ's reign ends?
options: He must put down all rule, authority, and power
He must judge the living nations
He must build his kingdom on earth
questions.correctAnswer: He must put down all rule, authority, and power
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 state that Christ must 'put down all rule and all authority and power' before delivering the kingdom to God the Father and that 'He must reign till he hath put all enemies under his feet.'

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 15:26 describe the 'last enemy' to be destroyed?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:26 clearly states, 'The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 15:27 reveal about all things being put under Christ's feet?
options: Christ is excepted who put all things under him
All things are under Christ including God the Father
Only earthly powers are under Christ
Christ has not yet been given authority
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is excepted who put all things under him
questions.explanation: Verse 27 says, 'it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him,' meaning God the Father put all things under Christ but Christ himself is not under anyone except the Father.

questions.question: What is the ultimate purpose described in 1 Corinthians 15:28 for the Son being subject to God the Father?
options: That God may be all in all
That the Son may reign forever
That the angels may worship the Son
questions.correctAnswer: That God may be all in all
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:28 states, 'then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.'

questions.question: What practical question does Paul raise in 1 Corinthians 15:29 regarding baptism?
options: Why are some baptized for the dead if the dead do not rise?
Why do some refuse baptism altogether?
Why is baptism necessary for salvation?
questions.correctAnswer: Why are some baptized for the dead if the dead do not rise?
questions.explanation: Verse 29 questions the practice: 'Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?'

questions.question: What reason does Paul give in 1 Corinthians 15:30 for standing in jeopardy every hour?
options: Because of persecution from the Jews
questions.explanation: Paul argues that risking his life constantly only makes sense if the resurrection is true, as indicated in the context of verses 29-31.

questions.question: How does Paul describe his daily experience in 1 Corinthians 15:31?
questions.explanation: Paul says, 'I die daily,' emphasizing his continual suffering for the sake of the gospel (1 Corinthians 15:31).

questions.question: What attitude does Paul caution against in 1 Corinthians 15:33?
options: Greed is the root of all evil
questions.explanation: Verse 33 warns, 'Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners,' teaching the importance of guarding one's associations.

questions.question: What exhortation is given in 1 Corinthians 15:34 for those lacking knowledge of God?
options: Awake to righteousness, and sin not
questions.correctAnswer: Awake to righteousness, and sin not
questions.explanation: Verse 34 commands, 'Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God,' calling for moral awakening and avoidance of sin.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 15:35 indicates some will question how the dead are raised and with what body they come.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:35 says, 'But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?' confirming this doubt is addressed.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 15:36, the body that is sown is the same one that shall be raised.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:36 states, 'that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die,' indicating the raised body differs from the sown body.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 15:39 teaches that all flesh is the same flesh, regardless of species.
questions.explanation: Verse 39 clarifies, 'All flesh is not the same flesh,' distinguishing between flesh of men, beasts, fishes, and birds.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 15.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:42-44, how is the resurrection body described in contrast to the natural body?
options: It is sown in dishonour and raised in glory
It is sown in incorruption and raised in corruption
It is sown a spiritual body and raised a natural body
It is sown in power and raised in weakness
questions.correctAnswer: It is sown in dishonour and raised in glory
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:42-44 describes the resurrection body as being sown in corruption, dishonour, and weakness but raised in incorruption, glory, and power, and specifically states there is a natural body and a spiritual body.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 15:45, who is described as the 'last Adam' and what is his nature?
options: The last Adam was made a quickening spirit
The last Adam was made a living soul
The last Adam was made of dust from the earth
The last Adam was made a natural body
questions.correctAnswer: The last Adam was made a quickening spirit
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:45 contrasts the first man Adam as a living soul with the last Adam being made a quickening (life-giving) spirit.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 15:50 say about 'flesh and blood' and inheriting the kingdom of God?
options: Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God
Flesh and blood will inherit the kingdom of God
Only flesh can inherit the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:50 explicitly states that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:51-52, what event will occur 'in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye'?
options: The trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised incorruptible
The stars will fall from heaven
The earth will be destroyed by fire
questions.correctAnswer: The trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised incorruptible
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:51-52 describes a mystery where 'we shall all be changed' in a moment, at the last trump, when the trumpet sounds and the dead are raised incorruptible.

questions.question: What is the literary contrast made between the first man and the second man in 1 Corinthians 15:47?
options: The first man is of the earth, earthy; the second man is the Lord from heaven
The first man is spiritual; the second man is natural
The first man is immortal; the second man is mortal
The first man is incorruptible; the second man is corruptible
questions.correctAnswer: The first man is of the earth, earthy; the second man is the Lord from heaven
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:47 contrasts the first man as earthly and the second man as the Lord from heaven, highlighting their different origins and natures.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 15:54 describe the result when 'this corruptible shall have put on incorruption'?
options: Death is swallowed up in victory
The kingdom of God is established on earth
questions.correctAnswer: Death is swallowed up in victory
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:54 states that when corruptible puts on incorruption and mortal puts on immortality, the saying 'Death is swallowed up in victory' is fulfilled.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'incorruption' (ἀφθαρσία) in 1 Corinthians 15:42 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἀφθαρσία' (aphtharsia) used in 1 Corinthians 15:42 refers to the state of being imperishable or immortal, especially in the context of resurrection bodies.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Corinthians 15:45 to contrast Adam and Christ?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:45 uses typology by presenting Adam as a type of the natural man and Christ (the last Adam) as the type of the spiritual man who brings life, fulfilling Old Testament expectations.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in 1 Corinthians 15:55 with 'O death, where is thy sting?'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:55 directly quotes Hosea 13:14, which asks 'O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?', linking resurrection victory to Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with 1 Corinthians 15:23 about Christ as the firstfruits in resurrection?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:23 speaks of believers as the 'firstfruits of the Spirit,' which connects to 1 Corinthians 15:23's theme of Christ as the firstfruits of those who are resurrected.

questions.question: What precedes the description of the resurrection body in 1 Corinthians 15:42?
options: A comparison of celestial and terrestrial bodies
The testimony of witnesses of the risen Christ
An argument about baptism for the dead
An exhortation to steadfastness in the work of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison of celestial and terrestrial bodies
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:40 precedes 15:42 and compares celestial and terrestrial bodies, setting the stage for the description of resurrection bodies in 15:42-44.

questions.question: What Greek word in 1 Corinthians 15:53 describes what 'this corruptible must put on'?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 15:53, the Greek word 'ἀφθαρσία' (incorruption) describes what the corruptible must put on, meaning imperishability or immortality.

questions.question: Which literary technique is found in the repeated structure of 1 Corinthians 15:42-44 emphasizing contrasts between sown and raised bodies?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:42-44 uses parallelism by pairing contrasts between the sown and raised states in a repeated, balanced structure to emphasize transformation.

questions.question: In the cultural context of 1 Corinthians 15, what was the significance of Paul mentioning 'baptized for the dead' in verse 29?
options: It was an argument to affirm the resurrection of the dead
It was a practice Paul endorsed openly
It referred to a pagan ritual
It was a metaphor for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It was an argument to affirm the resurrection of the dead
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:29 references a practice some Corinthians did, which Paul uses as a rhetorical argument to affirm belief in resurrection, challenging skeptics.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 15:58, Paul encourages believers to be unmoveable and always abounding in the work of the Lord because their labor is in vain.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:58 states the opposite: believers are encouraged to be steadfast because 'your labour is not in vain in the Lord.'

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 15:3 teach about salvation?
options: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures
Salvation is by works of the law
Faith alone is insufficient for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:3 explicitly states that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, affirming substitutionary atonement as a foundational doctrine of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 15:22 teach about human sin and redemption?
options: In Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive
Sin is eradicated by human effort
All are born sinless and must choose evil
questions.correctAnswer: In Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:22 contrasts the universality of death through Adam with the universal potential for life through Christ, teaching original sin and redemption.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 15:44 teach about the resurrection body?
options: It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body
The resurrection body is identical to the earthly body
The soul alone is resurrected without a body
Resurrection bodies are temporary and mortal
questions.correctAnswer: It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:44 teaches that resurrection involves transformation from a natural (physical) body to a spiritual (glorified) body, foundational for Christian eschatology.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 15:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 highlights God’s grace as the enabling power for Paul’s apostleship and labor, showing divine grace as central to Christian ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 15:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 declares Christ’s reign until all enemies are subdued, demonstrating God’s sovereign rule over all creation and history.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 15:20 connect to the theme of resurrection in Isaiah?
options: Christ as the firstfruits anticipates the general resurrection promised in Isaiah
It denies any resurrection, contradicting Isaiah
It focuses solely on spiritual resurrection unrelated to Isaiah
It teaches reincarnation, unlike Isaiah's resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the firstfruits anticipates the general resurrection promised in Isaiah
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:20 presents Christ’s resurrection as the firstfruits, fulfilling Old Testament promises like Isaiah 26:19 about the resurrection of the dead.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 15:28 relate to the ultimate fulfillment of God's kingdom as described in Daniel?
options: The Son subjects all to the Father, fulfilling Daniel’s vision of God’s eternal kingdom
It denies God’s kingdom ever coming, unlike Daniel
It teaches a temporary kingdom unlike Daniel’s eternal kingdom
It presents a human kingdom replacing God’s kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The Son subjects all to the Father, fulfilling Daniel’s vision of God’s eternal kingdom
questions.explanation: Verse 28 describes the Son subjecting all to the Father so that God may be all in all, corresponding to Daniel's prophecy of God’s eternal dominion (Daniel 7:13-14).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 42 and 44 teach about resurrection bodies?
options: Bodies are sown corrupted and raised incorruptible; natural bodies become spiritual
Resurrection bodies remain corruptible but are glorified
Only souls are resurrected without bodies
Bodies do not change but souls are judged
questions.correctAnswer: Bodies are sown corrupted and raised incorruptible; natural bodies become spiritual
questions.explanation: Verses 42 and 44 together teach that resurrection involves transformation from corruptible natural bodies to incorruptible spiritual bodies.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 51 and 53 teach about the final transformation of believers?
options: All believers will be changed to incorruption and immortality at the last trumpet
Only some believers are changed, others remain corruptible
Believers die and remain mortal without transformation
Transformation is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: All believers will be changed to incorruption and immortality at the last trumpet
questions.explanation: Verses 51 and 53 teach that believers will experience a bodily transformation to incorruption and immortality at the last trumpet, a key eschatological doctrine.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 55 and 56 teach about the defeat of death and sin?
options: Death’s sting is sin; sin’s strength is the law; but victory is through Christ
Death is undefeated; sin is not related to death
Sin is defeated but death remains victorious
The law alone defeats sin and death
questions.correctAnswer: Death’s sting is sin; sin’s strength is the law; but victory is through Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 55 and 56 explain the relationship between death, sin, and the law, culminating in victory through Jesus Christ (verse 57).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the resurrection is a myth and Paul’s preaching is vain. What does 1 Corinthians 15:12-19 actually teach?
options: If there is no resurrection, then Christ is not risen and our faith is vain
The resurrection is optional and does not affect faith
Paul admits the resurrection is a metaphor only
Faith is valid even without resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: If there is no resurrection, then Christ is not risen and our faith is vain
questions.explanation: Verses 12-19 argue that denying resurrection undermines Christ’s resurrection and invalidates Christian faith and preaching.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 15:29 teach about baptism and the resurrection?
options: Baptism for the dead presupposes belief in the resurrection
Baptism for the dead is purely symbolic without resurrection implications
The dead cannot be baptized, negating resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism for the dead presupposes belief in the resurrection
questions.explanation: Verse 29 uses the practice of baptism for the dead as an argument for the resurrection, implying that the practice makes sense only if resurrection is true.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 15:57 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 57 thanks God who gives victory through Jesus Christ, emphasizing God’s attribute of granting triumph over sin and death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 15:47 and 48 teach about human nature and Christ’s nature?
options: The first man is earthy; the second man is from heaven, and believers bear the image of each accordingly
Both men are earthly and identical in nature
Christ is merely a perfected earthly man, not divine
Believers do not share Christ’s nature
questions.correctAnswer: The first man is earthy; the second man is from heaven, and believers bear the image of each accordingly
questions.explanation: Verses 47 and 48 contrast Adam’s earthy nature with Christ’s heavenly nature, teaching that believers reflect these respective images.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 15:33 prepare believers for sanctification in light of resurrection doctrine?
options: Evil communications corrupt good manners, so holiness is necessary with resurrection hope
Communications have no effect on sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Evil communications corrupt good manners, so holiness is necessary with resurrection hope
questions.explanation: Verse 33 warns believers to avoid bad influences as part of holy living, which aligns with the resurrection’s call to righteousness.
